werk/alice-coltrane-huntington-ashram-mo.text:
Huntington Ashram Monastery is Alice Coltrane's second solo album. She recorded it in May 1969 in the studio in her home in Dix Hills, New York. It was released that year on John Coltrane Records, which was later absorbed into Impulse! Records. She plays harp and piano, together with bassist Ron Carter and drummer Rashied Ali.

The first three pieces are for harp, the last three for piano. AllMusic hears a meditative atmosphere in the harp pieces and more free jazz in the piano pieces. According to All About Jazz, the harp pieces hover between calm and searching, with Carter's repeating, throbbing bass as the pivot. The author Max Brzezinski praises Turiya, which lets the listener float in a cloud of rich sounds and plays endless variations on a theme.
werk/alice-coltrane-huntington-ashram-mo.listen: Listen to Turiya and notice how the musicians each follow a slow tempo of their own, until together they find a shared sense of time.

werk/alice-coltrane-journey-in-satchidan.text:
The first four tracks were recorded in November 1970 in the studio that Alice Coltrane had at home in Dix Hills, New York. Isis and Osiris is a live recording from the Village Gate in Greenwich Village, from July of that year. Alongside her on harp and piano, the players included saxophonist Pharoah Sanders, bassist Cecil McBee and drummer Rashied Ali. The album forms a transition to her later, more personal work. The title and title track refer to Swami Satchidananda, with whom she had studied.

The tracks carry meaning. Shiva-Loka is the realm of Shiva, Stopover Bombay refers to a trip to India and Sri Lanka, and Something About John Coltrane builds on themes by her late husband. Isis and Osiris shows her interest in Middle Eastern and North African music. The tanpura brings Indian classical music into the sound. The album was praised by many critics. In 2020 Rolling Stone placed it at number 446 among the greatest albums.
werk/alice-coltrane-journey-in-satchidan.listen: Listen to Journey in Satchidananda and notice Alice Coltrane's harp and the tanpura, the Indian string instrument heard on the studio recordings.

werk/alice-coltrane-lord-of-lords.text:
Lord of Lords is Alice Coltrane's seventh solo album. She recorded it in July 1972 in California and it was released in 1973 on Impulse!, her last album for that label. She plays piano, organ, harp, timpani and percussion, with bassist Charlie Haden, drummer Ben Riley and a string orchestra that she conducts herself. It is the third album in a series with strings, after Universal Consciousness and World Galaxy.

It contains three of her own pieces, excerpts from Stravinsky's The Firebird and Going Home, an arrangement of Dvořák's Ninth Symphony. Producer Ed Michel recounted that she had the strings play in ways that they themselves did not think possible. Critics praised the drone, the space and the spiritual charge: Pitchfork called it perhaps her most ecstatic record.
werk/alice-coltrane-lord-of-lords.listen: Listen to Excerpt from the Firebird and notice how strings and organ together give Stravinsky's music a new colour.

werk/alice-coltrane-ptah-the-el-daoud.text:
Ptah, the El Daoud is the third solo album by pianist and harpist Alice Coltrane, released by Impulse! Records in September 1970. She recorded it on 26 January 1970 in the basement of her home in Dix Hills, New York. For the first time, wind players had a larger role: Pharoah Sanders and Joe Henderson play tenor saxophone on two pieces and alto flute on Blue Nile, on which she herself moves from piano to harp. Sanders is consistently heard on the right, Henderson on the left.

All the music is by her. Ptah is the Egyptian god and El Daoud means the beloved in Arabic. AllMusic calls the record a truly great album, and Pitchfork counts Turiya and Ramakrishna among her best piano playing on record. JazzIz places the album among the five essential records of 1970.
werk/alice-coltrane-ptah-the-el-daoud.listen: Listen to Ptah, the El Daoud and notice how the two saxophonists come from different sides, Sanders on the right and Henderson on the left.

werk/alicia-keys-girl-on-fire.text:
After The Element of Freedom in 2009, Alicia Keys went through three eventful years: she married producer Swizz Beatz, became a mother and took more of her own career into her own hands. Girl on Fire was released in November 2012 and was her first album on RCA, after her previous label J Records had been absorbed into the group. Work took place in studios in New York, Los Angeles, Jamaica and London, with, among others, Swizz Beatz, Babyface and Jeff Bhasker.

She above all wanted to write a good song rather than chase a fashionable beat. The result is a restrained R&B record full of piano songs, with excursions into electro, rock, reggae and hip hop. She wrote Brand New Me together with Emeli Sandé, and on Fire We Make the blues-rock guitarist Gary Clark Jr. plays. Reviews were largely positive, and the album won a Grammy for Best R&B Album.
werk/alicia-keys-girl-on-fire.listen: Listen to Not Even the King and notice how the piano carries the song while the production stays restrained.

werk/alicia-keys-songs-in-a-minor.text:
Alicia Keys began writing songs for this album at the age of fourteen. In 1996 she signed with Columbia, but the label wanted to mould her into the next teen pop star and brought in well-known producers. She therefore began recording on her own initiative in 1998, first in her bedroom in Harlem and later in the basement of a house in Queens, together with Kerry Brothers. Columbia rejected the recordings. Clive Davis bought out her contract, and the album finally came out on J Records in 2001. Despite the title, only two songs are in A minor.

The classically trained pianist wrote, arranged and produced most of it herself. The result is neo-soul with classical music, R&B, soul and jazz. Fallin' became a worldwide hit and A Woman's Worth reached the American top ten. Critics praised the singer's maturity, and the album won five Grammys, including Best R&B Album.
werk/alicia-keys-songs-in-a-minor.listen: Listen to Fallin' and notice the role of the piano and the voice, which together carry the song.

werk/alicia-keys-the-diary-of-alicia-key.text:
The Diary of Alicia Keys, released in November 2003 by J Records, was Alicia Keys's second album. After her successful debut Songs in A Minor, she had to deliver the dreaded second record. She began writing already during the tour and recorded in New York, with live instruments, including in her own studio KrucialKeys. She wrote and produced almost everything herself. The album works as a musical diary, above all about the complexity of relationships. The sound is traditional 1960s and 1970s soul, mixed with classical piano and hip hop. Kanye West produced You Don't Know My Name and Timbaland worked on Heartburn.

She wrote If I Ain't Got You early on, after the news of Aaliyah's death. The album received wide praise and won a Grammy for Best R&B Album. It reached number one in the United States and yielded three top ten hits.
werk/alicia-keys-the-diary-of-alicia-key.listen: Listen to If I Ain't Got You and notice how her voice and the piano follow each other in this bluesy ballad.

werk/alva-noto-transform.text:
Transform was released in September 2001 on the German label Mille Plateaux and is the second studio album by Alva Noto, the alias of Carsten Nicolai. In 2008 the label Raster-Noton reissued the record. The album is the first part of the Transall series, which also consists of the EPs Transrapid, Transspray and Transvision, made between 2001 and 2006.

The music consists of tightly organised electronic sounds in which rhythm plays the leading role. Reviewer Mark Richard-San wrote in Pitchfork that Nicolai's sense of rhythm is the first thing that stands out. He found the record successful within its own limits, but missed a spark that would make it great: no moments when you stop and listen more closely. For him, Transform was simply good.
werk/alva-noto-transform.listen: Listen to Module 1 and notice the rhythm: how does it hold together those short, tight sounds?

werk/amalia-rodrigues-com-que-voz.text:
In January 1969, Amália Rodrigues recorded the fado album Com que voz. It was released in March 1970 on EMI and Valentim de Carvalho. She was accompanied by Pedro Leal on viola and José Fontes Rocha on Portuguese guitar.

In Portugal the album reached number one on the chart of the Associação Fonográfica Portuguesa. Later it gained a permanent place in Portuguese overviews: in 2009 BLITZ.pt included it among the fifty best Portuguese albums of the past fifty years, and the newspaper Público chose it among the best. In 2011 Expresso wrote that it is regarded as the singer's perfect album. In 2010 a remastered reissue appeared with fifteen previously unreleased recordings.
werk/amalia-rodrigues-com-que-voz.listen: Listen to Com Que Voz and notice how the voice holds the attention, with only viola and Portuguese guitar as accompaniment.

werk/amalia-rodrigues-fado-portugues.text:
Fado Português is a fado album by Amália Rodrigues, released on Columbia in June 1965. It was recorded at the Valentim de Carvalho studio in Paço de Arcos. Domingos Camarinha played Portuguese guitar, and Castro Mota and Martinho d'Assunção played viola, the Portuguese acoustic guitar that accompanies the singing. The cover photograph was by Augusto Cabrita. Eight of the twelve songs were written by Alain Oulman, with lyrics by poets such as Luís Vaz de Camões, David Mourão-Ferreira and Alexandre O'Neill.

The album reached number one in Portugal and number two in France. In 2015, fifty years after its release, a two-disc edition appeared, with the twelve original tracks and unused versions from the recording sessions.
werk/amalia-rodrigues-fado-portugues.listen: Listen to Erros Meus, to words by Camões, and notice how her voice carries the story, accompanied by the guitars.

werk/amy-winehouse-back-to-black.text:
After her jazzy debut Frank, Amy Winehouse wrote this second album out of heartbreak. Her boyfriend Blake Fielder-Civil temporarily left her for an ex, and she wrote most of the songs in that period, about guilt, grief and broken hearts. She loved the pop and soul of the 1960s girl groups. In 2005 and 2006 she recorded with producers Salaam Remi in Miami and Mark Ronson in New York, together with the Dap-Kings, Sharon Jones's band. This produced a sound from the past, blended with contemporary R&B and neo-soul.

Rehab, You Know I'm No Good, Back to Black, Tears Dry on Their Own and Love Is a Losing Game were released as singles. Critics praised the songwriting, the sensitive singing and the production. The album won a Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album and is regarded as a key record in the popularity of British soul in the late 2000s.
werk/amy-winehouse-back-to-black.listen: Listen to Back to Black and notice how the 1960s feel of the accompaniment suits the bitterness of the lyrics.

werk/andrew-cyrille-nuba.text:
For this album, Andrew Cyrille came together in June 1979 in Milan with singer and poet Jeanne Lee and saxophonist Jimmy Lyons. It was released on the Italian label Black Saint. It is therefore not a standard jazz trio: Lee's voice is as central as the drums and the alto sax.

The two versions of Nuba are based on a poem that Lee wrote in June 1979 for Lyons and Cyrille. In These Last Days is an adaptation of a poem from 1973. The lyrics are printed in the booklet that comes with the record. Lee does not sing the words straight ahead, but stretches and repeats them and also uses wordless cries. The Penguin Guide to Jazz called the album almost a miniature opera, and one reviewer wrote that there was nothing conventional or predictable about it.
werk/andrew-cyrille-nuba.listen: Listen to In These Last Days and follow how Jeanne Lee stretches and repeats words, while saxophone and drums follow her.

werk/andrew-cyrille-something-in-return.text:
Something in Return is a duo record by alto saxophonist Jimmy Lyons and drummer Andrew Cyrille. They recorded it on 13 February 1981 at Soundscape in New York, but the album was not released until 1988, on the label Black Saint. Both came from the circle around Cecil Taylor. The Penguin Guide to Jazz calls Cyrille an orchestra in himself, who conjures up layered energy, and gave it three and a half stars.

The opening track is Take the A Train by Billy Strayhorn. One reviewer described it as a challenging exercise in improvisation, in which Lyons does not let go of the familiar theme but gives it a new twist each time.
werk/andrew-cyrille-something-in-return.listen: Listen to Take the A Train and notice how the familiar theme keeps sounding through while saxophone and drums approach it differently each time.

werk/andrew-cyrille-what-about.text:
This was the first album that drummer Andrew Cyrille recorded under his own name. He made it in August 1969 in Paris, during a week-long marathon session of the label BYG Actuel. In that same week, Archie Shepp, the Art Ensemble of Chicago and Sunny Murray, among others, recorded albums there.

It is a solo record for percussion, without other musicians. Each of the five pieces has a character of its own: the title song begins with metronomic precision, From Whence I Came leans on the tom-toms and includes vocal sounds, Rhythmical Space mainly lets the cymbals sound. Rims And Things focuses on the rims of the drums. Critics praised the space and the silences in his playing and found the record surprisingly accessible. One reviewer called it one of the most refreshing solo drum albums ever.
werk/andrew-cyrille-what-about.listen: Listen to Rhythmical Space and notice how many different sounds come out of the cymbals, and how the silences between the strokes carry the playing.

werk/andrew-cyrille-x-man.text:
X Man was recorded in May 1993 at Sear Sound in New York and released in 1994 on Soul Note. Drummer Andrew Cyrille plays here with flautist James Newton, guitarist Alix Pascal and bassist Anthony Cox. Each musician wrote two of the eight pieces, and the solos are fairly shared out. Scott Yanow found the music surprisingly soft and melodic for such improvisers, a subtle record that becomes more interesting with every listen.

The Penguin Guide to Jazz heard the flute and guitar adding a new palette of colours, closer to Cyrille's sense of melody, and found that he here shows one of his simplest and least dense ways of playing.
werk/andrew-cyrille-x-man.listen: Listen to E-Squat and notice how clearly the flute's theme sounds and how restrained the drumming stays beneath it.

werk/andy-summers-bewitched.text:
Bewitched is the second and last album by the English guitarists Andy Summers and Robert Fripp, released in 1984 by A&M Records. Like its predecessor I Advance Masked, it is instrumental, but it sounds more pop-oriented. Summers said it was about two guitarists who meet on another mountain and learn to work together. The only single, Parade, received a video but did not reach the charts.

The record uses electronic drums and many overdubs. Critics were divided. Two authors felt that the synthesizers displaced the guitar playing, while Greg Prato of AllMusic praised the strong guitar work and pointed to the 7/4 rhythm in Maquillage. In 2024 Summers called the album ahead of its time.
werk/andy-summers-bewitched.listen: Listen to Maquillage and notice how the rhythm shifts without sounding forced.

werk/andy-summers-i-advance-masked.text:
I Advance Masked is a 1982 album by the English guitarists Andy Summers and Robert Fripp. The two had known each other since the early 1960s in Bournemouth. When their bands, The Police and King Crimson, were briefly dormant, they came together to jam, and that led to this album. They recorded it at Arny's Shack in Parkstone, Dorset.

It consists of thirteen instrumental tracks. Each track began with just two guitars; here and there Summers added some bass, percussion or string synthesizer. There are no drums, but according to him you do not miss them. He described the music as partly very accessible and partly avant-garde. The cover is a painting by the American pop artist James Rizzi. The title song was released as a single, with Hardy Country on the B-side.
werk/andy-summers-i-advance-masked.listen: Listen to I Advance Masked and try to hear how the two guitars complement each other without any need for drums.

werk/andy-williams-lonely-street.text:
Lonely Street is Andy Williams's fifth studio album and was released at the end of 1959 on Cadence Records. The album grew up around the hit Lonely Street, a song from Nashville that label boss Archie Bleyer had heard at the Everly Brothers' home. Bleyer conducted the recording on 23 August 1959, and the single reached number 5 in the Billboard Hot 100. The album itself was put together during an engagement in New Orleans, with pianist Dave Grusin and guitarist John Abate.

The songs are about lost love and loneliness. The singer makes greater use of the low, misty register of his voice. One critic suspected that he was inspired by Frank Sinatra's concept albums, such as In the Wee Small Hours. Lonely Street was his first record on the Billboard albums chart and reached number 38. AllMusic gave it four and a half stars.
werk/andy-williams-lonely-street.listen: Listen to I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry and notice how the singer performs this country classic by Hank Williams in his low, soft register.

werk/andy-williams-to-you-sweetheart-alo.text:
This album was released in the late summer of 1959 on Cadence Records and was the fourth that Andy Williams made for that label. The theme is Hawaiian, fitting the admission of Hawaii as the fiftieth state of the United States. The Hawaiian Wedding Song had already been a single in 1958 and stayed on the chart for twenty weeks, with number eleven as its highest position. The hit was already on his previous album Two Time Winners and was not re-recorded. Blue Hawaii and Sweet Leilani, however, he did record again for this record.

Archie Bleyer, the head of Cadence and leader of the orchestra, did not opt for traditional Hawaiian instruments or musicians from the islands. He had an ordinary orchestra play arrangements in Hawaiian style. What counted, wrote an AllMusic reviewer, were the singer's warm performances, which made the album a romantic touchstone. Billboard called it a tasteful, quiet package of familiar Hawaiian themes.
werk/andy-williams-to-you-sweetheart-alo.listen: In Beyond the Reef, listen to how the orchestra evokes Hawaii without traditional island instruments and how the warm baritone voice carries the song.

werk/andy-williams-two-time-winners.text:
Two Time Winners is the third album that Andy Williams released on Cadence Records, in the spring of 1959. The title refers to songs that had already been successful twice or had succeeded in two ways. The album contains older songs in new arrangements, accompanied by the orchestra of Archie Bleyer, who was associated with all his earlier hits. The first single, Hawaiian Wedding Song, entered the Billboard Hot 100 at the end of 1958 and reached number eleven. Twilight Time was not released as a single until three years later and reached number 86.

Critics appreciated the light, sometimes exotic new versions. Billboard declared the record its Spotlight Winner of the Week, because old standards in new guises were becoming popular again. Another magazine wrote that the songs are treated with a modern beat and thereby prove their indestructibility. According to Music Vendor, the album appealed to adults and teenagers alike.
werk/andy-williams-two-time-winners.listen: In Twilight Time, listen to how a well-known old song is brought back with gentle accompaniment and a warm singing voice.

werk/anitta-ritmo-perfeito.text:
Ritmo Perfeito is the second studio album by the Brazilian pop singer Anitta, released by Warner Music Brasil on 3 June 2014. On the same day her first live album with DVD, Meu Lugar, was released. She had announced the DVD in July 2013, and new songs had been written especially for it. They also ended up on this album in a studio version.

The sound remains pop and electropop, but with more influence from funk melody and R&B. She worked with new writers, including the rapper Projota, who wrote Cobertor and Mulher. He and MC Guimê appear as guests. The first single Cobertor received a video on YouTube, and a month later Na Batida followed. The album went gold with the ABPD.
werk/anitta-ritmo-perfeito.listen: Listen to Cobertor and notice the contribution of guest rapper Projota alongside the singing.

werk/ann-peebles-i-can-t-stand-the-rain.text:
I Can't Stand the Rain is the fourth album by the Memphis soul singer Ann Peebles. It was released in 1974 on the Hi label and is her highest-charting record on the Billboard 200: number 155, for seven weeks. Willie Mitchell produced the album, and she wrote a large part of the songs together with her husband Don Bryant.

The title song reached number six on the R&B chart and number 38 on the Hot 100 in 1973. I'm Gonna Tear Your Playhouse Down, written by Earl Randle, also became an R&B hit. Playing on the record are Howard Grimes on drums, Wayne Jackson on trumpet and the Memphis Strings, a string section.
werk/ann-peebles-i-can-t-stand-the-rain.listen: Listen to I'm Gonna Tear Your Playhouse Down and follow the singer's voice: where does she sound restrained, where does she push through?

werk/ann-peebles-straight-from-the-heart.text:
Straight from the Heart is the third album by the Memphis soul singer Ann Peebles, released on the Hi label. Her previous record, Part Time Love, was her first to reach the American R&B albums chart. She then began work on this album at Royal Recording Studios in Memphis. She chose Willie Mitchell as producer and worked with songwriters such as Don Bryant, her partner and later her husband, and George Jackson. The Hi Rhythm Section, the label's house band, also plays on it. I Pity the Fool, recorded by Bobby Bland in 1961, became a minor hit.

Critics were positive. Richie Unterberger wrote that the album showed how Hi surpassed the Memphis soul of its rival Stax in the early 1970s. It was her first record on the Billboard 200.
werk/ann-peebles-straight-from-the-heart.listen: Listen to Trouble, Heartaches & Sadness and notice the opening line, which RZA later sampled for a song by Wu-Tang Clan.

werk/anne-dudley-songs-from-the-victorio.text:
Anne Dudley and Jaz Coleman wrote this 1990 album together. They recorded it in Cairo and London. The title refers to Cairo itself: the Arabic name of the city literally means the Victorious. The album falls under world music.

Dudley played keyboards, Coleman violin, cobra flute and transverse flute. In addition, musicians played instruments such as the qanun, the kawala, the nay and the accordion. Hossam Ramzy provided the percussion, and a string orchestra, the Cairo Strings, was conducted by Tareq Aakef. Western keyboards thus mingle with the sounds of the city after which the record is named. The album was later used as a source: in 1993 Enigma sampled extensively from it for two songs.
werk/anne-dudley-songs-from-the-victorio.listen: Listen to Habebe and try to hear which instruments you recognise, and how together they form a single whole.

werk/anneke-gronloh-brandend-zand.text: In July 1962 Brandend zand by Anneke Grönloh was released. She was born in 1942 in Tondano in the Dutch East Indies and spent her first years in a Japanese internment camp. The song is a translation by Johnny Hoes of the German Heißer Sand. It stayed at the top of the charts for weeks and is said to have sold more than three million copies worldwide. In 2000 Grönloh was named singer of the century.
werk/anneke-gronloh-brandend-zand.listen: Hear the exotic atmosphere of desert and longing, and Grönloh's warm, powerful voice.

werk/anouar-brahem-conte-de-l-incroyable.text:
This is the second album by the Tunisian oud player Anouar Brahem. He recorded it in October 1991 and it was released on ECM in May 1992. The title means Tale of an Incredible Love.

It is a quartet. Besides the oud we hear two wind players from Turkey, Barbaros Erköse on clarinet and Kudsi Erguner on ney, and percussionist Lassad Hosni on bendir and darbouka. That line-up gives the music a colour of its own, in which the strings of the oud and the breath of the wind instruments complement each other. The album opens with Étincelles and closes with a piece for ECM founder Manfred Eicher. AllMusic's review gave three stars and wrote that the record reveals more and more special moments on repeated listening.
werk/anouar-brahem-conte-de-l-incroyable.listen: Listen to Conte de l'incroyable amour and notice how the oud, the clarinet and the ney take turns leading.

werk/anouk-graduated-fool.text:
Graduated Fool is the third studio album by the Dutch singer Anouk, released on 22 November 2002. She produced the album herself, and she wrote most of the songs together with van Veen. It yielded three singles: Everything reached number 12 in the Dutch Top 40, Hail number 31 and I Live for You did not make the chart.

Promotion was limited, because she was pregnant with her son Elijah. The album reached number 3 on the Dutch albums chart. With about 25,000 copies sold, it was until then her least successful record.
werk/anouk-graduated-fool.listen: Listen to Everything, the single with the highest chart position from this album, and consider why this song worked best.

werk/anouk-hotel-new-york.text:
Hotel New York is the fourth studio album by the Dutch pop and rock singer Anouk, released on 3 December 2004. The title refers to the hotel in Rotterdam where she wrote all the songs.

The album entered at number one in the Netherlands and stayed in that position for twelve weeks. It spent 87 weeks on the chart and went triple platinum. It also reached number one in Belgium. The singles Girl, Lost and One Word all reached number two in the Dutch Top 40, and Jerusalem reached number twenty.
werk/anouk-hotel-new-york.listen: Listen to Girl, the first single from the album, and consider why this song rose so high on the chart.

werk/anouk-together-alone.text:
Together Alone is the debut album of the Dutch singer Anouk. It was produced by Barry Hay and George Kooymans of the rock band Golden Earring, together with John Sonneveld, who was also the sound engineer. Hay and Kooymans also sing and play on it. We also hear Tren van Enckevort on accordion, John Legrand on harmonica, Lex Bolderdijk and Frank Carillo on guitar and Michel van Schie on bass guitar, among others.

The album was very successful in the Netherlands and yielded three singles in the top 30: Nobody's Wife, It's So Hard and Sacrifice. The record has eleven tracks, from Nobody's Wife to the closing number Mood Indigo. There is also a compilation edition with a second disc containing a remix of Nobody's Wife and video clips of two songs.
werk/anouk-together-alone.listen: Listen to Nobody's Wife and try to hear which instruments sound alongside the voice.

werk/anouk-urban-solitude.text:
Urban Solitude is the second studio album by the Dutch pop and rock singer Anouk Teeuwe, from 1999. She produced it herself, with Ronald Trijber as co-producer and engineer. The idea for the cover is also hers. She wrote the music and lyrics together with Bart van Veen, who worked on eleven of the thirteen songs.

The record yielded four singles. R U Kiddin' Me reached number two on the Dutch chart, Michel number three, The Dark number eight and Don't number thirteen. In the Netherlands the album went platinum, in Belgium gold. On My Best Wasn't Good Enough, Dinand Woesthoff sings along. The album has thirteen tracks, from In the Sand to My Friend.
werk/anouk-urban-solitude.listen: Listen to My Best Wasn't Good Enough and notice the second voice of Dinand Woesthoff alongside the singer's.

werk/anthony-braxton-five-pieces-1975.text:
Five Pieces 1975 was recorded on 1 and 2 July 1975 at Generation Sound Studios in New York and released on Arista. Anthony Braxton plays several instruments here: sopranino and alto saxophone, clarinet, contrabass clarinet, flute and alto flute. He was accompanied by trumpeter Kenny Wheeler, bassist Dave Holland and drummer Barry Altschul. In 2008 Mosaic Records included the record in the box set The Complete Arista Recordings of Anthony Braxton.

The album mixes a well-known standard with original compositions. You Stepped Out of a Dream is by Nacio Herb Brown and Gus Kahn. The other pieces are by Braxton himself and bear composition numbers such as 23H, 23G, 23E and 40M. The piece 23E lasts well over seventeen minutes. Scott Yanow gave the record four and a half stars and praised the tight, alert group and the strength of the compositions.
werk/anthony-braxton-five-pieces-1975.listen: Listen to You Stepped Out of a Dream and notice how the quartet plays a well-known standard, before the long original pieces that follow.

werk/anthony-braxton-for-alto.text:
Anthony Braxton recorded For Alto in 1969, in the basement of the Parkway Community Center in Chicago. The album was released in 1971 on Delmark Records. He plays everything on alto saxophone, with no other musicians and no overdubs. Other jazz musicians had occasionally recorded an unaccompanied solo, but this was the first jazz album to consist entirely of solo alto.

Braxton was inspired by the piano music of Schoenberg, Fats Waller and Stockhausen, but found his own piano playing too weak and therefore created a language of his own for the saxophone. After a solo concert in 1967 in which he ran out of ideas after ten minutes, he mapped out elements such as long tones, trills and multiphonics as a springboard for improvisation. He called this Language Music. The first reactions were divided: some found it revolutionary, others an ego trip. Later the album was recognised as a milestone, and it inspired other saxophonists to make solo albums.
werk/anthony-braxton-for-alto.listen: Listen to To Composer John Cage and notice how a single saxophone alternates long tones, fast flourishes and silences, without accompaniment.

werk/anthony-braxton-new-york-fall-1974.text:
New York, Fall 1974 was recorded in the autumn of 1974 at Generation Sound Studios in New York, on 27 September and 16 October, and released on Arista. All the music is by Anthony Braxton himself. He plays sopranino saxophone, alto saxophone, clarinet, contrabass clarinet and flute. On four tracks he is accompanied by trumpeter Kenny Wheeler, bassist Dave Holland and drummer Jerome Cooper. In 2008 the record was also released in the box set The Complete Arista Recordings of Anthony Braxton by Mosaic Records.

The line-up changes from piece to piece. Richard Teitelbaum plays Moog synthesizer in Composition 38 A, and in Composition 37 a saxophone quartet is heard with Julius Hemphill, Oliver Lake and Hamiet Bluiett. Leroy Jenkins plays violin in the last piece. Scott Yanow gave the record four stars and called the great variety a perfect introduction to Braxton's complicated but logical music.
werk/anthony-braxton-new-york-fall-1974.listen: Listen to 30-EGN (Opus 37) and notice how the saxophones play with one another, without a rhythm section underneath.

werk/anthony-braxton-trio-and-duet.text:
Anthony Braxton recorded this album in 1974 for the Canadian label Sackville. It shows him in two settings: a trio with an original composition and three duets on jazz standards. In the trio, trumpeter Leo Smith and Richard Teitelbaum on Moog synthesizer play along. In the duets, Dave Holland plays bass. He uses alto saxophone, clarinet and contrabass clarinet, and also chimes and bass drum.

The record contains The Song Is You, Embraceable You and You Go to My Head, alongside the long opening piece Composition 36. Delmark Records reissued the album in 2015 with two bonus tracks, On Green Dolphin Street and I Remember You. The AllMusic reviewer gave it four stars. Critics later called it one of the best records he made in the 1970s, and proof of his many-sided vision.
werk/anthony-braxton-trio-and-duet.listen: Listen to Embraceable You and notice the interplay of saxophone and bass. Try to hear how freely both musicians treat the familiar melody.

werk/antonio-carlos-jobim-orfeu-da-conce.text:
Orfeu da Conceição began as a play with music by the poet Vinicius de Moraes and the composer Antônio Carlos Jobim, which premiered in Rio de Janeiro in 1956. The play transposes the Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice to a contemporary favela during carnival. The soundtrack was released in the same year on a 10-inch LP on Odeon. It is regarded as the first album of songs by the duo Jobim and De Moraes, who together wrote the seven numbers for the play.

Jobim orchestrated the music and conducted Le Grand Orchestre Odeon, an orchestra of 35 musicians. Luiz Bonfá plays guitar, Roberto Paiva sings the songs and De Moraes himself declaims Orpheus's monologue. The record was recorded in hi-fi. The play later became the basis for the 1959 film Orfeu Negro.
werk/antonio-carlos-jobim-orfeu-da-conce.listen: Listen to Monólogo de Orfeu: here there is no singing, but Vinicius de Moraes declaims and dramatises the text.

werk/antonio-carlos-jobim-the-composer-o.text:
The Composer of Desafinado, Plays, from 1963, is Antônio Carlos Jobim's first album under his own name. It contains twelve instrumental arrangements of his own songs, arranged by Claus Ogerman. That was the beginning of a lifelong collaboration between the two. Jobim plays guitar and piano. The producers mainly wanted to show the Latin man with his guitar and objected to the piano, as the cover also shows.

The album opens with The Girl from Ipanema. In 1964 a recording of that song by Astrud Gilberto and Stan Getz became a worldwide hit. It also includes Corcovado, Desafinado and Chega de Saudade, nearly all of them jazz standards. Down Beat wrote that this record alone would fully justify the bossa nova. In 2001 the album was inducted into the Latin Grammy Hall of Fame, and in 2007 Rolling Stone Brasil placed it at number 58 among the hundred best Brazilian records.
werk/antonio-carlos-jobim-the-composer-o.listen: Listen to The Girl from Ipanema and notice how the melody is played by instruments instead of sung. Can you hear what the strings add to it?

werk/aphex-twin-drukqs.text:
Drukqs was released on 22 October 2001 on Warp Records and is a double album by Aphex Twin. He released it after leaving an MP3 player containing 180 unpublished tracks behind on an aeroplane. To get ahead of a leak he made an album of it himself, also because it was to be his last release for Warp. Many titles are in Cornish or in code. According to him, the title is an invented word.

The record shifts in style: fast programmed rhythms from jungle and drum and bass, ambient, electro-acoustic pieces and piano music, played on computer-controlled instruments such as a modified Yamaha Disklavier. Critics heard prepared piano in the line of John Cage and piano pieces reminiscent of Erik Satie. The album was one of his most controversial: some found it not very innovative, others praised it as a skilful work. Avril 14th is one of his best-known recordings.
werk/aphex-twin-drukqs.listen: Listen to Avril 14th, one of his best-known recordings, and notice how different a piano piece sounds from the fast rhythms elsewhere on this record.

werk/aphex-twin-richard-d-james-album.text:
In 1995, under the name AFX, Richard D. James had already experimented with fast, exaggerated rhythms on the Hangable Auto Bulb EPs, inspired by drum and bass and by his friend Luke Vibert. The 1996 album, released by Warp Records, he made largely on his Macintosh, and it took more time than his earlier records. His method for the drums: he tapped out the rhythm on the keyboard and then spent four hours shifting the notes into the right place.

The record sets lightning-fast breakbeats against lovely strings and ambient melodies. For the strings he bought a violin at a flea market and sampled individual notes. In To Cure a Weakling Child, his voice, distorted by the computer, sounds like a child giving a lecture. Critical reception was glowing, especially about the production. It became Warp's best-selling release to that point, and is counted among the best albums of the 1990s.
werk/aphex-twin-richard-d-james-album.listen: Listen to To Cure a Weakling Child. Notice the distorted, childlike voice and how it moves against the complicated rhythms.

werk/aphex-twin-selected-ambient-works-8.text:
The debut was released in November 1992 on Apollo, an ambient label of the Belgian R&S Records. Richard D. James recorded the music between 1985 and 1992, from the age of thirteen or fourteen, with home-built synthesizers and drum machines on cassette. His first EP, Analogue Bubblebath, caught R&S's attention. He came to Belgium with a box full of cassettes, from which they chose tracks. According to James, they were songs that his friends found nice to relax to.

The sound is ambient techno, with rhythms from techno and acid house and melodies that are delicate and atmospheric. The opening track Xtal sounds hazy and dreamy. Pulsewidth is suited to the dance floor, Green Calx has metallic clanks and hum. Critics called the record a classic that broadened ambient and brought techno to fans of indie music. In 2012 the magazine Fact declared it the best album of the 1990s.
werk/aphex-twin-selected-ambient-works-8.listen: Listen to Xtal and notice the hazy melody and the muffled woman's voice above the calm rhythm.

werk/aphex-twin-selected-ambient-works-v.text:
After the success of his debut, Aphex Twin signed with Warp Records, where this album was released in March 1994. Richard D. James recorded it largely in 1993 in his studios in London and Cornwall, with old synthesizers by EMS, Moog and ARP, among others. He said he was inspired by lucid dreams: after waking up he tried to recreate the sounds. He himself compared it to standing in a power station under the influence of LSD.

Unlike his debut, the record consists almost entirely of ambient without beats. The music sounds cold, empty and threatening, and uses microtonal tunings. Most tracks had no title, and were given abstract photographs instead. Critics were divided on release, mainly because of the repetition. Later the record was praised, and in 2016 Pitchfork placed it second among the best ambient albums ever.
werk/aphex-twin-selected-ambient-works-v.listen: Listen to Blue Calx: notice the calm, almost empty sound, and how little changes while the piece slowly moves on.

werk/aphrodite-s-child-666.text:
Aphrodite's Child's third and last album was a double album with a grand concept: a contemporary reading of the biblical Book of Revelation. Vangelis wrote the music and film director Costas Ferris the lyrics. In the story a circus re-enacts the apocalypse, while outside the tent the real apocalypse is taking place, until the two coincide. Recording began at the end of 1970 at Europa Sonor in Paris and lasted a little over three months. The atmosphere was tense, because the other band members would rather have stuck to the psychedelic pop music that had brought their success.

The record company refused to release the album, partly because of the track written with the infinity symbol as its title, which Vangelis cut down from 39 to five minutes. Meanwhile the group broke up and the album was not released until June 1972. Reviews and sales were lukewarm, but later it gained cult status and became the group's most acclaimed work, with a place on lists of the best progressive rock albums.
werk/aphrodite-s-child-666.listen: Listen to Aegian Sea and notice how the music resembles a cinematic sound world more than a pop song.

werk/arcade-fire-funeral.text:
Arcade Fire recorded its debut album largely in one week in August 2003, at Hotel2Tango in Montreal, entirely analogue. It was finished in 2004, including in the apartment of Régine Chassagne and Win Butler. The production is estimated to have cost around ten thousand dollars. During the work, several relatives of band members died. That gave the album its title and its themes: death, change and the loss of innocence.

The first half forms the Neighborhood suite, about a city without power in the middle of winter, based on the ice storm of 1998. Rebellion (Lies) became the most successful single. Pitchfork gave the album a 9.7, and the reviews were largely glowing. It received a Grammy nomination and appeared on many lists of the best albums of the 2000s. According to Stereogum it was perhaps the most influential indie rock album of its time.
werk/arcade-fire-funeral.listen: In Wake Up, listen to how the song slowly builds and the choir grows ever larger. Notice how communal and exuberant it sounds.

werk/arcade-fire-neon-bible.text:
After Funeral, which had been recorded in an attic studio, Arcade Fire wanted a permanent place to record. The band bought the Petite Église in Farnham, Quebec, a former church and Masonic temple that had served as a café, and recorded most of the album there in the second half of 2006. Michael Pärt made additional recordings in Budapest with a film orchestra and a military men's choir. Nick Launay mixed the tracks. It was the first album with drummer Jeremy Gara and violinist Sarah Neufeld as permanent members.

The sound is heavy and menacing, with orchestra, choir, hurdy-gurdy, mandolin, accordion and pipe organ. Win Butler was inspired by TV preachers and by the feeling of looking at his home country from the outside. (Antichrist Television Blues) and Black Mirror are among the core tracks. Reviews were largely glowing, although some magazines found it too bombastic. The album entered at number two on the American chart and was regarded as an example of the rise of indie rock.
werk/arcade-fire-neon-bible.listen: Listen to Black Mirror, one of the first songs to emerge for the album, and notice the menacing, full sound.

werk/arcade-fire-reflektor.text:
Reflektor came about between 2011 and 2013, in Montreal, in Jamaica and in Louisiana. The occasion was a trip by Win Butler and Régine Chassagne to Haiti, her family's country, where rara music deeply affected the band. The album was largely recorded on analogue tape. Alongside regular producer Markus Dravs, the band worked with James Murphy of LCD Soundsystem. There were sixty song ideas and eighteen long tracks, so it became a double album.

The music is art rock and dance rock, with lyrics in English and French. Butler was inspired by the film Black Orpheus and by an essay by Kierkegaard. Here Comes the Night Time and Here Comes the Night Time II are about twilight in Port-au-Prince. Supersymmetry was originally intended for the film Her. The reviews were positive, and in 2014 Pitchfork included the album on a list of the best albums of the decade so far.
werk/arcade-fire-reflektor.listen: Listen to Reflektor and notice how danceable the song is, and hear how many layers there are in the sound.

werk/arcade-fire-the-suburbs.text:
The Suburbs is Arcade Fire's third album and was released on 3 August 2010 on Merge Records. The producer was Markus Dravs. The lyrics go back to the childhood of Win and William Butler in The Woodlands, a suburb of Houston, Texas. According to Win Butler, the album is neither a love letter to the suburbs nor an indictment, but a letter from the suburbs. It was recorded in the home of Win Butler and Régine Chassagne in Montreal, partly also in Quebec and New York. He described the sound as a mix of Depeche Mode and Neil Young.

The band first pressed each song onto a 12-inch lacquer and then recorded it again for the digital master. The album received glowing reviews and topped the charts in Canada, the United States and the United Kingdom, among others. In 2011 it won the Grammy for Album of the Year, a Juno Award and the Polaris Music Prize.
werk/arcade-fire-the-suburbs.listen: Listen to We Used to Wait and notice the piano and the nostalgic tone in which the song looks back on the past.

werk/archie-shepp-fire-music.text:
Fire Music was released in 1965 on Impulse! Records. Malcolm, Malcolm Semper Malcolm is dedicated to Malcolm X, and Los Olvidados is a tribute to the 1950 film of the same name. Besides Archie Shepp on tenor saxophone, the players are trumpeter Ted Curson, trombonist Joe Orange, alto saxophonist Marion Brown, bassist Reggie Johnson and drummer Joe Chambers. The CD edition adds a live track, recorded at the Village Gate on 28 March 1965.

In the piece for Malcolm X, the leader himself recites a text. Bassist David Izenzon and drummer J.C. Moses play on it. There are also two pieces by others: Prelude to a Kiss by Ellington and The Girl from Ipanema. AllMusic found the album somewhat uneven but recommended. All About Jazz called it challenging and yet accessible to most listeners.
werk/archie-shepp-fire-music.listen: Listen to Malcolm, Malcolm Semper Malcolm and notice the spoken text by the saxophonist and the different line-up from the rest of the record.

werk/archie-shepp-four-for-trane.text:
Four for Trane was tenor saxophonist Archie Shepp's first album for Impulse! in 1965. It came about thanks to John Coltrane, who put in a good word with producer Bob Thiele after an evening at the Half Note. Thiele set one condition: the group had to play Coltrane's music. Four of the five pieces are by Coltrane and were rewritten by the saxophonist and the trombonist Roswell Rudd. The band had rehearsed for months, and the recording went almost take by take. Coltrane came to listen himself and was co-producer.

Also playing are Alan Shorter on flugelhorn, John Tchicai on alto saxophone, bassist Reggie Workman and drummer Charles Moffett, among others. The Penguin Guide to Jazz counts the record as part of its core collection. Critics wrote that the arrangements do not repeat the pieces, but make something new of them.
werk/archie-shepp-four-for-trane.listen: Listen to Naima, a piece by Coltrane, and notice how this group makes it its own.

werk/archie-shepp-mama-too-tight.text:
Mama Too Tight was released in 1967 on Impulse! Records. The music was recorded on 19 August 1966 at Van Gelder Studio in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. Archie Shepp played tenor saxophone in a large, unusual line-up: trumpeter Tommy Turrentine, trombonists Grachan Moncur III and Roswell Rudd, tuba player Howard Johnson, clarinettist Perry Robinson, bassist Charlie Haden and drummer Beaver Harris.

The opening piece takes up an entire side. A Portrait of Robert Thompson (as a young man) lasts almost nineteen minutes and includes a piece by Duke Ellington and two traditional melodies. The other side has the title track, Theme for Ernie and Basheer. An AllMusic reviewer hears a composer who has found his stride: free blowing, angry outbursts and exuberant cries are balanced by Ellingtonian elegance and restraint.
werk/archie-shepp-mama-too-tight.listen: In Mama Too Tight, listen to the many horns and try to hear when the playing is free and when the melody runs on calmly.

werk/arctic-monkeys-favourite-worst-nigh.text:
This second album was recorded quickly at Miloco Studios in East London, with producers James Ford and Mike Crossey. The band wanted to get back on tour and half of the songs had already been played live. Bassist Andy Nicholson had left shortly after the debut; Nick O'Malley took his place. The album sounds more ambitious than Whatever People Say I Am, That's What I'm Not: faster, harder and with a fierce production, with ambient sounds and more elaborate drum rhythms. The band had by now travelled the world, and you can hear it.

Brianstorm opened as the first single, and Fluorescent Adolescent also became a hit. The organ at the beginning of the closing track 505 refers to Ennio Morricone's music for The Good, the Bad and the Ugly. Critics praised the emotional depth and the more mature lyrics of Alex Turner. The album won a Brit Award and is regarded as the beginning of the change of sound that the band carried through on every subsequent album.
werk/arctic-monkeys-favourite-worst-nigh.listen: Listen to 505 and notice the organ at the beginning, which evokes a film soundtrack by Ennio Morricone.

werk/arctic-monkeys-whatever-people-say-.text:
Arctic Monkeys formed in 2002 and handed out free demo CDs at gigs. Fans put the music online, and so demand grew among the public, the press and the record industry before there was even an official album. Eight of the songs were already freely available on the internet by the end of 2004. The debut was released in January 2006 on Domino, after the number one singles I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor and When the Sun Goes Down. It is the only album with bassist Andy Nicholson.

The music mixes indie rock, garage rock and post-punk revival. The lyrics sketch the nightlife of young northern Englishmen, told by the nineteen-year-old Alex Turner. From the Ritz to the Rubble is about bouncers, Red Light Indicates Doors Are Secured about the search for a taxi after a night out. The title comes from a novel by Alan Sillitoe. The album became the fastest-selling debut album in British history and won the Mercury Prize.
werk/arctic-monkeys-whatever-people-say-.listen: In Red Light Indicates Doors Are Secured, listen to how the lyrics tell a night spent looking for a taxi as a short scene. Notice the small details of everyday life.

werk/aretha-franklin-i-never-loved-a-man.text:
This 1967 album was the first that Aretha Franklin made for Atlantic Records. At Columbia she had not broken through after eight albums of jazz standards. The title song was recorded at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, but after a quarrel between her then husband Ted White and studio owner Rick Hall the session broke up. Producer Jerry Wexler continued the recording in New York, where members of the Muscle Shoals rhythm section were also flown in.

The single Respect, an adaptation of a song by Otis Redding, reached number 1 in the Billboard Hot 100 and became her trademark. The title song reached the top 10. The album reached number 2 on the American albums chart. The first reactions were mixed, but appreciation later grew enormously. In 2020 Rolling Stone placed it at number 13 among the 500 greatest albums ever.
werk/aretha-franklin-i-never-loved-a-man.listen: Listen to Respect and notice how she takes over Redding's song and makes it her own. Can you hear how assertive her voice sounds?

werk/aretha-franklin-lady-soul.text:
Aretha Franklin released Lady Soul in January 1968 on Atlantic Records. It was her twelfth studio album. Jerry Wexler produced and Tom Dowd engineered it. On several tracks, backing singers join in: Cissy Houston with her group the Sweet Inspirations, and Franklin's sisters Carolyn and Erma. On Good to Me As I Am to You, Eric Clapton can be heard on guitar.

The album contains a number of her biggest hits: Chain of Fools, (You Make Me Feel Like) A Natural Woman and (Sweet Sweet Baby) Since You've Been Gone. It spent sixteen weeks at the top of Billboard's R&B albums chart and reached number two on the pop albums chart. It sold more than a million copies in the United States and later appeared in lists of the greatest albums of all time, including those of Rolling Stone and Pitchfork.
werk/aretha-franklin-lady-soul.listen: In Chain of Fools, listen to the power of the voice and to the backing vocals around it.

werk/aretha-franklin-laughing-on-the-out.text:
Aretha Franklin was twenty-one when she made this fourth studio album for Columbia Records. It was released on 12 August 1963 and recorded at Columbia Recording Studios in New York and Hollywood. She sang jazz and pop standards, from Johnny Mercer to Duke Ellington, accompanied by arrangements by Columbia producer Robert Mersey.

One of the best-known songs is her version of Skylark. About two minutes after the start, she sings the word Skylark with power and feeling. On this album she also recorded one of her first own compositions: I Wonder (Where Are You Tonight). The album is somewhat overlooked in her Columbia catalogue. In June 2008 it was reissued, together with The Electrifying Aretha Franklin on a single release.
werk/aretha-franklin-laughing-on-the-out.listen: Listen to Skylark and notice the moment after almost two minutes when the singer delivers the title word with great power.

werk/ariana-grande-sweetener.text:
After Dangerous Woman in 2016, Ariana Grande began her next album in July of that year. The first song to emerge was the title song, which Pharrell Williams wrote and produced. She recorded more than thirty songs that did not make the album. Sweetener was the first album on which she took the lead in the writing herself. Her manager spoke of a more mature sound.

The album was released on 17 August 2018 and is mainly pop, R&B and trap, with influences from house, funk and neo-soul. It opens with a short a cappella version of Raindrops (An Angel Cried), originally by Frankie Valli and the Four Seasons. No Tears Left to Cry, God Is a Woman and Breathin all reached the top fifteen of the American Hot 100. Critics praised the experimental production. The album won the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album, her first Grammy.
werk/ariana-grande-sweetener.listen: Listen to raindrops (an angel cried) and notice how a short a cappella opening, without instruments, begins the album.

werk/ariana-grande-yours-truly.text:
Work on this debut album began in August 2010, during the filming of the series Victorious. In 2011 Ariana Grande signed with Republic Records. The songs took shape over almost two years, with Harmony Samuels, Babyface and Leon Thomas III among the producers. She was dissatisfied with the first direction and wanted to make the music she herself had grown up with: 1990s urban pop.

The sound is pop and R&B, with influences from 1990s hip hop, 1950s piano pop and doo-wop. She named Mariah Carey, Whitney Houston, Amy Winehouse and Christina Aguilera as inspirations. The record opens with Honeymoon Avenue, a quiet song in doo-wop style. The Way, with Mac Miller, was the first single and reached number nine in the American Hot 100. Critics particularly praised her singing.
werk/ariana-grande-yours-truly.listen: Listen to Honeymoon Avenue and notice how 1950s doo-wop is mixed with an urban sound.

werk/armin-van-buuren-a-state-of-trance.text: On 18 May 2001 ID&T Radio broadcast the first episode of A State of Trance, the radio show of DJ Armin van Buuren from Leiden. Every week he mixed two hours of new trance, dance music with long build-ups and floating melodies. The programme grew into one of the biggest DJ shows in the world, with tens of millions of listeners in more than eighty countries.
werk/armin-van-buuren-a-state-of-trance.listen: Hear how the track slowly builds with floating synthesizers and a voice that keeps returning.

werk/armin-van-buuren-mirage.text:
Mirage is the fourth studio album by the Dutch DJ and producer Armin van Buuren. It was released on 10 September 2010 on Armada Music. The first single, Full Focus, was released on 24 June 2010.

The many guests are characteristic of the album. Singer Sophie Ellis-Bextor, singer Christian Burns, singer Nadia Ali, producer BT, Ferry Corsten and Adam Young of Owl City collaborated on it. In the Netherlands the album entered at number 3. In the United States it appeared on the Billboard 200 and on the dance and electronic chart. The deluxe edition also contains a DVD with video clips.
werk/armin-van-buuren-mirage.listen: Listen to Feels So Good with Nadia Ali and notice how the singing voice and the electronic sounds together carry the song.

werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-a-jackson-i.text:
In 1969 the Art Ensemble of Chicago recorded this album for the French label BYG Actuel. The four musicians are Lester Bowie on trumpet, Joseph Jarman and Roscoe Mitchell on saxophones, clarinets and percussion, and Malachi Favors Maghostut on bass. On the 1989 CD, The Waltz was replaced by a live fragment, Hey Friend, which did not return in later editions.

Critics mainly heard the players' backgrounds reflected: free improvisation, European modern classical music, attempts to incorporate African music and a strongly theatrical streak. AllMusic gave the record four and a half stars and called it entertaining and carefree. JazzTimes pointed to the circus-like title song, to Ericka, a spoken piece with marimba, and to Song for Charles, a long, lyrical tribute to the late Charles Clark.
werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-a-jackson-i.listen: Listen to Ericka and notice how the spoken text and the marimba together create a cool, charged atmosphere.

werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-fanfare-for.text:
Fanfare for the Warriors is a studio album by the Art Ensemble of Chicago, released on the Atlantic label. The regular line-up is Lester Bowie, Joseph Jarman, Roscoe Mitchell, Malachi Favors Maghostut and Don Moye. They are joined by pianist Muhal Richard Abrams, the leader of the AACM, the Chicago collective from which the group emerged.

All seven pieces are by one of the members: Favors wrote Illistrum, Bowie Barnyard Scuffle Shuffle, Jarman the title track and What's to Say, and Mitchell Nonaah, Tnoona and The Key. Each piece thus has a character of its own. The reviewer Scott Yanow of AllMusic saw in the record the conclusion of the group's first, and probably most important, period. He called it a fine calling card for this important avant-garde group.
werk/art-ensemble-of-chicago-fanfare-for.listen: Listen to Nonaah and notice how the horns alternate in a piece that Mitchell wrote and that has an atmosphere of its own beside the rest of the record.
